title: Barcelona and Brazil winger Raphinha facing five weeks out with hamstring injury
content:
Barcelona are set to be without winger Raphinha for around five weeks after the Brazilian suffered a hamstring injury on international duty.

“Raphinha has a right hamstring injury, as confirmed by medical tests carried out by the Brazilian Football Federation (CBF) following the discomfort he experienced during the Brazil v France match in Boston on Thursday,” Barca said in a statement on Friday evening.

“The player is returning to Barcelona to begin the appropriate treatment. The estimated recovery time is five weeks.”

Brazil confirmed that the 29-year-old, alongside Roma full-back Wesley, had both been dropped from the national team squad due to injuries during the defeat to France.

A statement from Brazil read: “On Friday, the athletes underwent imaging tests that confirmed muscle injuries. The players are free to continue their treatment. No other athletes will be called up to replace them.”

Raphinha’s injury is a major blow for Barcelona. The versatile forward is integral to manager Hansi Flick’s plans, and has scored 19 goals and provided eight assists in 31 games this season.

The former Leeds United forward has spent time on the sidelines due to hamstring injuries this season, first missing almost two months of action with an issue in September before a more minor issue left him unavailable in February.

Barcelona, four points clear at the top of La Liga, are next in action against fourth-placed Atletico Madrid on April 4.

They face Atletico again in the quarter-finals of the Champions League, with the first leg being played at the Camp Nou on April 8 and the return leg at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano on April 14.

Hansi Flick has a problem. He is losing the player he considers to have been his most important, and during the most crucial stage of the season.

A tough Champions League quarter-final awaits Barca against Atletico Madrid, the side that knocked them out of the Copa del Rey in the semi-finals (4-0 in the first leg and 3-0 in the second leg).

Barça’s attack is not in top form. Flick’s approach of splitting playing time 50-50 between Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres has left both players lacking in confidence, and when the Brazilian has been injured this season, the team has struggled to score goals. Marcus Rashford started the season well, but now seems to have hit a bit of a rough patch.

Without Raphinha, the team relies on the brilliance of Lamine Yamal, but Barca lose a goalscorer and one of their most pressing players. Two key elements for the end of the season.
